subject.title: Feature/Fix: Integrate lineage discovery and shadow accounting

question: Should the repository land the four-PR lineage stack in order, or first adopt the narrower fork identity and cache-invalidation path from https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118?
rationale: Both paths address the same overcount investigation with different scope, and automated review cannot safely choose the permanent scanner architecture or landing sequence.

options.title: Stage the lineage stack
options.body: Merge the prerequisite, require exact-head cold and warm proof here, and explicitly reconcile the narrower PR before reviewing later slices.

options.title: Land the narrower fix first
options.body: Adopt the proof-positive identity and cache repair, then rebase and reduce the lineage stack to behavior that remains necessary.

options.title: Pause the rearchitecture
options.body: Keep the production scanner on narrower fixes until the lineage approach demonstrates sufficient accuracy and operational value to justify its complexity.

recommendation.title: Stage the lineage stack
recommendation.body: Merge the prerequisite, require exact-head cold and warm proof here, and explicitly reconcile the narrower PR before reviewing later slices.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is best positioned to select the scanner architecture and coordinate overlapping landing candidates.
